goblinPackingEdit:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this existing transparent 4-column by 4-row goblin sprite sheet. Preserve the exact goblin design, rounded head proportions, vest, boots, wooden club, colors, all 16 animation poses, and transparency.
There is ONE packing error: the goblin in ROW 2 COLUMN 3 (the forward club-swing attack pose, counting from 1) extends its club left across its cell boundary into ROW 2 COLUMN 2. Fix only this packing problem.
Move the entire ROW 2 COLUMN 3 character INCLUDING its whole club slightly right, by approximately 2% of the full image width, so its full silhouette is comfortably inside that one cell with at least 5% of a cell of fully transparent margin on every side. If needed shrink ONLY this character and its equipment uniformly by 5% to achieve the margin, preserving its body aspect ratio. Its feet baseline must stay aligned with the other attack frames.
Remove the stray portion of this same club which currently intrudes into the right edge of ROW 2 COLUMN 2. Preserve the actual character and raised club in ROW 2 COLUMN 2 unchanged.
All other 14 cels must keep their current design, pose, scale, position and visual quality. Keep the canvas square and the exact equal 4×4 grid, with no gutters or visible grid lines. No new shapes, text, marks, backgrounds, shadows or effects. True transparent PNG.

prompts.mushroom:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production pixel-art character animation sheet for a small game HUD, not a design presentation. Reference image 1 is the approved CHARACTER DESIGN. Preserve the subject's silhouette, proportions, colors and details faithfully.
Output a square PNG with TRUE TRANSPARENT background, exactly FOUR equal columns and FOUR equal rows (16 animation cels). Each cel is exactly one quarter of the image in both directions. Absolutely no gutter, border, cell lines, labels, text, background or drop shadow. All cels have matching size, camera and character identity. Crisp pixel clusters, dark navy pixel outline, restrained colors, clean pixel-art shading, no blur or airbrush. Target the readable detail of a 64×64 pixel character, enlarged as pixel art; do not simplify into a low-detail icon.
Every character is horizontally centered at 50% of its cel and its feet/body baseline remains at 88% cel height. The entire character, limbs and equipment fit within x=8%..92% and y=8%..88% of each cel. Never crop the head, feet or wing/weapon tips. Keep identical body volumes in all poses. Character faces the viewer, slightly toward screen left.
Row 1: FOUR distinct rhythmic idle dance poses, leaning left, dipping, leaning right, recovering, with articulated body parts and head lag; seamless loop. A subtle dance, no big jumps.
Row 2: FOUR ordered attack cels: ready, anticipation, attack toward screen left, recover.
Row 3: FOUR ordered hit cels: surprised impact, recoil with squeezed eyes, buckling, dazed rest. Gentle/cartoon, no gore.
Row 4: the same FOUR idle poses as row 1, with slightly more stern eyes/eyebrows and a tiny warm-red accent; same body and proportions. Keep the change subtle.
Only ONE full character in each of exactly 16 evenly spaced cells. No other characters, floor, scenery, projectiles, text, stars, sparkles or glow.
SUBJECT AND SPECIFIC MOTION: The CORAL RED MUSHROOM in the TOP LEFT of reference image 1. Preserve the wide rounded red cap with THREE irregular cream spots and a shaded warm-brown underside, plump cream stem/body with two dark rectangular eyes, and little brown feet. The stem/body is large enough to read as the chubby face, not a tiny stick below a floating cap. Idle: cap tilts and body gently compresses as feet rock in place. Attack: a tiny forward cap headbutt, then recover. Maintain the same wholesome friendly design as the reference.

prompts.goblin:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production game sprite animation sheet, not a presentation board.
Reference image 1 is a CHARACTER DESIGN reference. Reproduce ONLY the green GOBLIN at bottom right, keeping its rounded tall head, long pointed ears, stocky body, brown vest/shorts, expressive narrow dark eyes, chunky wooden club, leaf-green skin, and dark navy pixel outline. The reference's proportions and charm must survive; do not squash the head or replace the body with a thin stick.
Create a square 1024×1024 PNG with TRUE TRANSPARENT background, exactly FOUR equal columns and FOUR equal rows (16 cels). Each cel is exactly 256×256 with no gutter, border, labels or dividers. Every cel uses the same virtual 64×64 pixel grid enlarged 4× with nearest-neighbor style: clean flat pixel clusters, no antialiasing, no gradients, no blur. Pixel art quality like the reference, with readable hands, vest opening, broad face, short boots and a chunky club. Limited muted green, warm brown, cream highlights and navy outline.
Align EVERY character at cell center x=128 and planted feet baseline y=224. Character bounding box including ears and club fits x=24..232, y=24..224. Same body volume and same camera/front three-quarter pose in every cel, facing slightly toward screen left (opponent looks toward player). Keep a stout head approximately as tall as its face is wide, excluding ears; reference image is the authority.
ROW 1: four rhythmic grounded idle dance poses, waist swaying left then right, knees gently dipping, head lagging, club bobbing; feet stay on baseline. Each pose distinct, seamless loop.
ROW 2: attack sequence: ready stance, club raised, swing club toward screen left, recover. All limbs and the whole club stay within the cel.
ROW 3: hit sequence: surprised impact, recoil with squeezed eyes, knees buckling, dazed crouch; no gore, no disappearing parts.
ROW 4: same four idle dance poses as row 1, with subtly more stern eyebrows and tiny warm-red cheek accent; retain identical character design and proportions.
Exactly ONE full goblin in each of 16 evenly spaced cells. No other characters, no text, no background, no floor, no shadow, no glow. Do not flatten or simplify the approved character into a low-detail icon.
